key_insight: PEA organic spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects, slowing ambient light- and heat-induced degradation compared with BA spacers in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection can improve perovskite durability, but long-term device stability also requires surface passivation, encapsulation, and performance trade-off optimization.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 exfoliated nanoflakes.
Evaluated light and thermal stability under ambient conditions.
Probed degradation using confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Fresh nanoflakes showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract reports material-level stability rather than solar-cell efficiency or device lifetime, and describes no AI method.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
